question: Imports of small South African citrus fruits into the EU have surged by 117 per cent over five marketing years, to 169 904 tonnes in the 2025–2026 season up to July, according to official data from the Spanish Ministry of Agriculture.

The rising numbers of such fruit on the EU market in September and October coincides with the start of the European season, putting pressure on prices at source and making it hard to sell early-season varieties. Against this backdrop, the Valencian Community has lost 16 334 hectares of mandarin orchards since 2015, a sign of the parlous state of this sector, whose profitability is thus being jeopardised.

Farmers’ organisations are calling for Article 34 of the EU-SADC Economic Partnership Agreement to be invoked. This provides for safeguard measures in the event of market turmoil or harm to European producers. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission believe the bilateral safeguard under Article 34 needs to be invoked to address the surge in South African imports and their impact on European production?
What actions and timetable does it envisage for ascertaining the need for and, where appropriate, adopting these measures?
Is it willing to take urgent provisional measures to prevent further harm to European producers until such time as this procedure is completed?
